name: Simon
overview: Simon, also known as Simon Iscariot, is a male figure identified primarily as the father of Judas. His tribal affiliation is not recorded in Scripture. There are no additional notes about his life or character beyond his paternal relationship to Judas.
namesAndTitles: The name Simon means 'he has heard' or 'obedient one,' reflecting a common Hebrew name of the period. The surname Iscariot indicates he was a man from Kirioth. Together, these names identify him specifically as Simon from Kirioth, distinguishing him within the Gospel narrative.
familyAndRelationships: Simon is noted in Scripture as the father of Judas, according to John 6:71. No other family relationships are recorded for him beyond this paternal connection.
scriptureSignificance: Simon’s significance in the biblical narrative is tied entirely to his son Judas, who is a prominent figure in the New Testament. While Simon himself is not directly involved in the events recorded, his identification as Judas’s father provides important genealogical context. This connection situates Judas within a known family line, contributing to the fuller understanding of Judas’s background.
